3. Enter your new credit card information.
4. Click **Update**.


# Downgrade your billing plan
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/downgrade-billing-plan

Downgrade your Pinecone organization from a paid plan to the free Starter plan, including plan requirements, index limits, and billing impact.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To change your billing plan, you must be an [organization owner or billing admin](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles).

> [!TIP]
>
> If you're on the Standard plan with credit/debit card billing and want to reduce spend without returning to the free Starter plan, consider [switching to the Builder plan](#switch-from-standard-to-builder) for a flat \$20/month.

## Before you downgrade

When you downgrade to the Starter plan in the Pinecone console, you choose which projects, indexes, assistants, and members to keep. You can keep up to the [Starter plan limits](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits): 1 project, 5 serverless indexes in the `us-east-1` region of AWS, 5 assistants, and 2 members. Pinecone deletes everything you don't keep, along with all backups, backup schedules, and collections.

The downgrade doesn't reduce your data or change your configuration, so do this first:

* **Move any serverless indexes outside the `us-east-1` region of AWS that you want to keep.** [Create a new index](/guides/index-data/create-an-index) in `us-east-1`, [re-upsert your data](/guides/index-data/upsert-data), and delete the old index before you start the downgrade. Indexes in other [regions](/guides/index-data/index-configuration#cloud-regions) can't be kept on Starter.
* **Migrate any dedicated read node indexes** whose data you want to keep. They can't run on Starter and there's no self-serve conversion. If the index is in `us-east-1`, [back it up](/guides/manage-data/back-up-an-index) and [restore it](/guides/manage-data/restore-an-index) (this creates a new on-demand serverless index in the same region), then delete the original and keep the restored index during the downgrade. If it's in another region, create a new `us-east-1` index and re-upsert your data as described above. You can also [contact Support](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/support/ticket) to migrate back.
* **Migrate any pod-based indexes** whose data you want to keep. [Migrate each one to serverless](/guides/indexes/pods/migrate-a-pod-based-index-to-serverless) and finish creating the new serverless index before you start the downgrade, because the migration saves your index as a collection and the downgrade deletes all collections.
* **Move any `eu`-region assistants you want to keep to `us`.** [Recreate them in `us`](/guides/assistant/create-assistant) and re-upload their files. `eu` assistants you don't move are deleted.
* **Disconnect your organization's [SSO connection](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-single-sign-on-sso).**
* **Reassign or remove members** whose [organization role](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) isn't available on the Starter plan.
* **Get under the Starter storage limits.** Starter allows no more than 2 GB of data across your serverless indexes and 1 GB of assistant storage. Do this last, after the migrations above, because they can briefly leave a second copy of an index. [Delete records](/guides/manage-data/delete-data) and [assistant files](/guides/assistant/manage-files#delete-a-file) to fit.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You don't need to bring [Assistant usage](/guides/assistant/pricing-and-limits) (ingestion units, chat tokens, and context tokens) under Starter caps before downgrading. If you exceed Starter limits after downgrading, new requests may be blocked until usage is within limits.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you're switching from Standard to Builder instead of Starter, your organization must be under the [Builder plan quotas](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits). You must also delete all backups and remove or stop any features not available on Builder, such as bulk import, pod-based indexes, storage integrations, RBAC, and SSO.

## Downgrade to the Starter plan

The downgrade process is different depending on how you're paying for Pinecone.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Start the downgrade in the Pinecone console, as described below. The console walks you through what to keep and cleans up the rest. If you start the downgrade in a cloud marketplace instead, that cleanup doesn't run, so Pinecone deactivates your account and you'll need to [contact Support](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/support/ticket).

> [tab] Credit card
>
> 1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
> 2. Click **Downgrade** in the **Starter** plan section.
>
> Your billing ends immediately, but you'll receive a final invoice for any charges accrued in the current month.

> [tab] Google Cloud Marketplace
>
> 1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
> 2. In the **Starter** section, click **Downgrade**.
> 3. Click **Confirm downgrade**.
> 4. On the **Continue your downgrade on GCP Marketplace** modal, click **Continue to marketplace**. This takes you to your orders page in Google Cloud Marketplace.
> 5. [Cancel the order](https://cloud.google.com/marketplace/docs/manage-billing#saas-products) for your Pinecone subscription.
>
>    > [!TIP]
>    >
>    > If you don't see the order, check that the correct billing account is selected.
>
> Your billing ends immediately, but you'll receive a final invoice for any charges accrued in the current month.

> [tab] AWS Marketplace
>
> 1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
> 2. In the **Starter** section, click **Downgrade**.
> 3. Click **Confirm downgrade**.
> 4. On the **Continue your downgrade on AWS Marketplace** modal, click **Continue to marketplace**. This takes you to the [Manage subscriptions](https://console.aws.amazon.com/marketplace) page in the AWS Marketplace.
> 5. [Cancel the subscription](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/cancel-subscription.html#cancel-saas-subscription) to Pinecone.
>
> Your billing ends immediately, but you'll receive a final invoice for any charges accrued in the current month.

> [tab] Microsoft Marketplace
>
> 1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
> 2. In the **Starter** section, click **Downgrade**.
> 3. Click **Confirm downgrade**.
> 4. On the **Continue your downgrade on Azure Marketplace** modal, click **Continue to marketplace**.
> 5. On the **SaaS** page, click your subscription to Pinecone.
> 6. Click **Cancel subscription**.
> 7. Confirm the cancellation.
>
> Your billing ends immediately, but you'll receive a final invoice for any charges accrued in the current month.

## Switch from Standard to Builder

If you're on the Standard plan and pay by credit/debit card, you can switch to the [Builder plan](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits) for a flat \$20/month:

1. Bring your organization under the [Builder plan quotas](/reference/api/database-limits). In particular, you must be within the Builder plan limits for projects, indexes, namespaces, storage, users, and monthly usage units.
2. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
3. Click **Switch to Builder** in the **Builder** plan section.
4. Confirm the change.

After switching, overages are no longer billed. Instead, requests that exceed Builder quotas are blocked. If you need more capacity, [upgrade back to Standard or Enterprise](/admin/billing/upgrade-billing-plan) at any time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The [Builder plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) is available with credit/debit card billing only and isn't supported through cloud marketplaces.

If you pay through a cloud marketplace, you can't switch to the Builder plan at this time. [Contact Support](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/support/ticket) to be notified when this migration becomes available.


# Download a usage report
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/download-usage-report

Download a usage and cost report for your Pinecone organization from the console, or export one with the Admin API.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To view usage and costs across your Pinecone organization, you must be an [organization owner or billing admin](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles). Also, this feature is available only to organizations on the Standard or Enterprise plans.

The **Usage** dashboard in the Pinecone console reports usage and costs across your organization. On the page you can group the charts by SKU or project and switch the cost distribution between services. The CSV download covers whichever time range you select, regardless of how you group the charts.

> [tab] Pinecone console
>
> 1. In the top-right navigation of the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Usage**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/usage).
> 2. Select the time range to report on. This defaults to the current month, or to the previous month during the first five days of a month.
> 3. Click **Download**.
>
>    On Standard plans, the report downloads right away.
>
>    On Enterprise plans, choose **Download CSV** from the menu. The export runs in the background and appears in the list on the page. When it finishes, click **Click to download** on its entry.
>
>    > [!TIP]
>    >
>    > The download provides more granular detail than the console view, including breakdowns by individual index as well as project and index tags.
>
> On Enterprise plans, exports you create through the Admin API appear in that same list.

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > Exporting through the Admin API is available only on [Enterprise plans](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) and requires an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).
>
> Exporting with the Admin API takes three requests: create the export, poll it until it finishes, then download the file.
>
> **1. Create the export**
>
> An export covers whole UTC calendar days, each written as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `period_start` is the first day you want and can be no earlier than 365 days before today. `period_end` is the day *after* the last day you want, so `2026-08-01` through `2026-09-01` covers all of August. Omit the request body to export the trailing 30 complete days.
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
>
> curl -X POST "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/cost-usage-exports" \
>      -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
>      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>      -d '{
>            "period_start": "2026-08-01",
>            "period_end": "2026-09-01"
>          }'
> ```
>
> The export is recorded but hasn't run yet, so the response returns `"status": "Pending"` and the file fields are empty:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": "9f2c1a4e-8b3d-4c5f-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a7b8",
>   "status": "Pending",
>   "format": "zip",
>   "period_start": "2026-08-01",
>   "period_end": "2026-09-01",
>   "data_available_through": null,
>   "row_count": null,
>   "size_bytes": null,
>   "download_url": null,
>   "download_url_expires_at": null,
>   "file_expires_at": null,
>   "file_expired": false,
>   "error": null,
>   "created_at": "2026-09-02T14:31:07.482910355Z",
>   "started_at": null,
>   "finished_at": null,
>   "updated_at": "2026-09-02T14:31:07.482910355Z"
> }
> ```
>
> An organization can run only one export at a time. Starting another while one is `Pending` or `InProgress` returns a `409`. An organization can also start at most five exports per hour. Going over that returns a `429` with a `Retry-After` header.
>
> **2. Poll until the export finishes**
>
> Use the `id` from the previous step to check on the export.
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> EXPORT_ID="9f2c1a4e-8b3d-4c5f-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a7b8"
>
> curl -X GET "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/cost-usage-exports/$EXPORT_ID" \
>      -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN"
> ```
>
> `status` moves from `Pending` to `InProgress`, and then to either `Completed` or `Failed`. Both of those are terminal and never change afterward. When the export completes, the response carries the file's size, row count, and download link:
>
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "id": "9f2c1a4e-8b3d-4c5f-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a7b8",
>   "status": "Completed",
>   "format": "zip",
>   "period_start": "2026-08-01",
>   "period_end": "2026-09-01",
>   "data_available_through": "2026-08-31",
>   "row_count": 48213,
>   "size_bytes": 4183902,
>   "download_url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/example-bucket/cost_usage_exports/export.zip?X-Goog-Expires=3600&X-Goog-Signature=abc123",
>   "download_url_expires_at": "2026-09-02T15:36:11.237604891Z",
>   "file_expires_at": "2026-09-04T14:35:52.904155718Z",
>   "file_expired": false,
>   "error": null,
>   "created_at": "2026-09-02T14:31:07.482910355Z",
>   "started_at": "2026-09-02T14:31:19.118374902Z",
>   "finished_at": "2026-09-02T14:35:52.904155718Z",
>   "updated_at": "2026-09-02T14:36:11.237604891Z"
> }
> ```
>
> `data_available_through` is the date of the most recent usage row in the export. Because cost data lags behind usage, it can be earlier than the `period_end` you asked for.
>
> **3. Download the file**
>
> `download_url` is a signed link to a zip archive. The archive holds the cost records as one or more CSV files whose columns follow the [FOCUS v1.4](https://focus.finops.org/) Cost and Usage dataset. Each CSV starts with a header line and holds at most 800,000 rows, so a large export is split across several files, named `part-1-of-3.csv` through `part-3-of-3.csv` and ordered by those names. The numbers are zero-padded once an export runs to ten or more parts, so a 12-part export starts at `part-01-of-12.csv`.
>
> The archive also holds a `manifest.json` listing the export's window, `row_count`, the 45 column names, and each part with its own row count.
>
> FOCUS uses its own names for the things being billed, so Pinecone's organization, project, and index appear under FOCUS columns rather than under the headings you see in the console:
>
> | Pinecone | FOCUS columns |
> | - | - |
> | Organization | `x_OrganizationId` for the ID, `BillingAccountName` for the name |
> | Project | `SubAccountId`, `SubAccountName` |
> | Resource | `ResourceId`, `ResourceName`, with `ResourceType` naming the kind |
>
> `BillingAccountId` holds your billing customer ID, which isn't the same as your Pinecone organization ID.
>
> Most rows describe an index, but an export also covers other resources, so `ResourceType` can be `index`, `assistant`, `backup`, `collection`, or `model`. Rows for fixed fees leave it empty.
>
> Columns prefixed with `x_` are Pinecone extensions, which is how FOCUS requires a provider to name a column the specification doesn't define. For the full column list, see [Create a cost usage export](/reference/api/latest/admin/cost-usage-exports/create-a-cost-usage-export).
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> DOWNLOAD_URL="YOUR_DOWNLOAD_URL"
>
> curl -o cost-usage-export.zip "$DOWNLOAD_URL"
> ```
>
> Pinecone generates a new link each time you read a single export, and each link is valid for one hour. `download_url_expires_at` tells you when the current one stops working. To get a fresh link, read the export again. Treat the link as a secret while it's valid, since anyone who has it can download the file.
>
> Pinecone deletes the file itself two days after the export finishes, and you can't download it again. Check `file_expired` rather than `status` to know whether the file is still there, because a `Completed` export whose file has expired can no longer be downloaded. Create another export instead.
>
> To see the exports your organization has already run, use [List cost usage exports](/reference/api/latest/admin/cost-usage-exports/list-cost-usage-exports). List responses always return `download_url` as `null`, so read a single export when you need a link.

Dates are shown in UTC to match billing invoices. Cost data is delayed up to three days from the actual usage date.


# Account deactivation for non-payment
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/non-payment-account-deactivation

Learn what happens when Pinecone deactivates an account for non-payment, how long data is retained, and how to reactivate.

If your organization has continued non-payment on a paid billing plan, Pinecone may deactivate your account. While your account is deactivated, you can't use Pinecone services, but your data is retained for a limited time so you can reactivate and recover it.

## Data retention after deactivation

When your account is deactivated for non-payment:

* Your account data is retained for 30 days from deactivation.
* After 30 days, all account data is permanently deleted. This action can't be undone.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This 30-day retention period applies specifically to accounts deactivated for continued non-payment. Other deletion flows, such as when you [delete resources](/guides/production/data-deletion) or [end your relationship with Pinecone](/guides/production/data-deletion), follow different retention timelines described in the [data deletion policy](/guides/production/data-deletion).

When your account is deactivated, organization owners see this notice in the Pinecone console:

> **Your account has been deactivated**
>
> Due to an unresolved payment issue, your account was deactivated and all running indexes have been archived. Please update your payment information to reactivate.

Other organization members see a message asking them to contact an organization owner.

## Reactivate your account

To reactivate your account and preserve your data before the 30-day retention period ends:

1. Sign in to the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io).
2. Go to [**Settings > Billing > Overview**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing).
3. Update your payment information or resolve the outstanding balance.

Organization [owners and billing admins](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) can update billing details. For help changing how you pay, see [Change your payment method](/admin/billing/change-payment-method).

## API access while deactivated

API requests may fail with a [402 - Payment Required](/reference/api/errors#402---payment-required) response while your account has a payment issue or is deactivated for non-payment. After you reactivate your account, retry your requests. For general error-handling guidance, see [Error handling](/guides/production/error-handling).

## Contact support

If you believe your account was deactivated in error, [contact Support](https://www.pinecone.io/contact/support/) or [open a support ticket](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/support/ticket) from the console.

## See also

* [Change your payment method](/admin/billing/change-payment-method)
* [Data deletion on Pinecone](/guides/production/data-deletion)
* [Billing disputes and refunds](/admin/billing/billing-disputes-and-refunds)


# Redeem a promo code
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/redeem-a-promo-code

Learn how to redeem a Pinecone promo code when you upgrade to the Builder plan, and how to fix common redemption errors.

Pinecone promo codes, also called discount codes, discount the Builder plan. You enter a code while upgrading an organization from Starter to Builder, and you can't add one after the organization is on a paid plan.

## Before you start

Each code works for one email address and one plan, and only until its redemption date.

* Sign in with the email address the code was sent to. The code doesn't work for anyone else, even a teammate in the same organization.
* Select the organization you want to discount. The code applies to whichever organization is selected when you upgrade. To switch, click the organization name at the top left of the console.
* Make sure that organization is on the Starter plan and isn't in an active [Standard trial](/admin/billing/standard-trial).
* Make sure you're an organization owner or billing admin. Other [organization roles](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) can't change the plan.
* Make sure the code hasn't expired. Codes look like `BUILDER-20261231-0A1B2C3D4E5F`, where the 8-digit date is the last day you can redeem it, in UTC.

## Redeem a code

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. In the **Builder** plan section, click **Upgrade**.
3. In the **Continue on Builder** dialog, click **Add discount code**.
4. Paste your code and click **Add code**. Letter case and extra spaces don't matter.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. Enter your credit or debit card information and click **Upgrade**.

The dialog shows **Discount code applied** for any code you add, valid or not. Pinecone checks the code when you click **Upgrade**, and if the code is rejected, the upgrade doesn't go through and you aren't charged.

## After you redeem a code

When the upgrade succeeds, the console confirms that your discount code has been applied. The cost table in the upgrade dialog still shows the full \$20/month, because the discount is applied to your [invoices](/admin/billing/access-your-invoices).

While the discount is active, the plan card on [**Settings > Billing > Overview**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing) shows the date it ends. Pinecone emails you 5 days before that date and again when the discount ends. After that, Builder is billed at the regular price.

The discount only applies to the Builder plan. If you move the organization to another plan, the discount ends. If the upgrade dialog offers a Builder launch promotion, your code replaces it.

## Troubleshoot redemption errors

| Message or symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| "Failed to upgrade. Discount code is not valid for this account." | The code has a typo, is for a plan other than Builder, or was sent to a different email address than the one you're signed in with. | Paste the code exactly as you received it, and check that it starts with `BUILDER-`. Sign in with the email address the code was sent to. |
| "Failed to upgrade. Discount code has expired." | The redemption date in the code has passed. | [Contact support](/admin/support/contact-support) if you think the code should still be valid. |
| "Failed to upgrade. A subscription already exists for this organization." | The selected organization is already on a paid plan. | Select an organization on the Starter plan. To discount an existing subscription, [contact support](/admin/support/contact-support). |
| The Add discount code link is missing | The organization isn't on Starter or is in an active Standard trial, or you clicked **Upgrade** on a plan other than Builder. | Check which organization is selected and its current plan, and then click **Upgrade** in the **Builder** plan section. |
| The Upgrade button is disabled | You aren't an owner or billing admin, or the organization is billed through a cloud marketplace. | Ask an organization owner to upgrade or to give you the billing admin role. If the organization is billed through a cloud marketplace, [contact support](/admin/support/contact-support). |

## Contact support

[Contact support](/admin/support/contact-support) if you upgraded without entering your code, applied it to the wrong organization, or your code was sent to an email address you don't use to sign in. Include the code, the organization name, and the email address you sign in with.


# Pinecone Standard plan trial
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/standard-trial

Evaluate the Pinecone Standard plan with $300 in credits over 21 days, including bulk import, backup and restore, RBAC, and higher scale limits.

The Standard trial lets you evaluate Pinecone without any up-front payment. You get \$300 in credits over 21 days with access to Standard plan [features](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) and [limits](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits) that are suitable for testing Pinecone at scale.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you're building a small or personal project, consider the free [Starter plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) or the flat-rate [Builder plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) instead.

## Key features

* \$300 in credits
* 21 days of access to Standard plan [features](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/), including:
  * [Bulk import](/guides/index-data/import-data)
  * [Backup and restore](/guides/manage-data/backups-overview)
  * [RBAC (role-based access control)](/admin/security/security-overview#role-based-access-controls-rbac)
* [Higher limits](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits) for testing at scale
* Access to all [cloud regions](/guides/index-data/index-configuration#cloud-regions)
* Access to [Developer Support](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/?plans=support)

## Expiration

When your Standard trial ends, or when you use all of your credits, your quotas are blocked and console access is limited to the billing page. You don't automatically return to your previous plan. To restore full access, do one of the following:

* Add a payment method and continue on the Standard plan.
* Upgrade to the Enterprise plan.
* [Downgrade to the Starter plan](#downgrade-to-the-starter-plan) (you can also do this any time before the trial expires).

If you started the trial from the Builder plan, you aren't charged the \$20/month Builder fee during the trial.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Learn more about [pricing](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/).

## Downgrade to the Starter plan

You can downgrade from a Standard trial to the Starter plan at any time.

When you downgrade to the Starter plan in the Pinecone console, you choose which projects, indexes, assistants, and members to keep. You can keep up to the [Starter plan limits](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits): 1 project, 5 serverless indexes in the `us-east-1` region of AWS, 5 assistants, and 2 members. Pinecone deletes everything you don't keep, along with all backups, backup schedules, and collections.

The downgrade doesn't reduce your data or change your configuration, so do this first:

* **Move any serverless indexes outside the `us-east-1` region of AWS that you want to keep.** [Create a new index](/guides/index-data/create-an-index) in `us-east-1`, [re-upsert your data](/guides/index-data/upsert-data), and delete the old index before you start the downgrade. Indexes in other [regions](/guides/index-data/index-configuration#cloud-regions) can't be kept on Starter.
* **Migrate any dedicated read node indexes** whose data you want to keep. They can't run on Starter and there's no self-serve conversion. If the index is in `us-east-1`, [back it up](/guides/manage-data/back-up-an-index) and [restore it](/guides/manage-data/restore-an-index) (this creates a new on-demand serverless index in the same region), then delete the original and keep the restored index during the downgrade. If it's in another region, create a new `us-east-1` index and re-upsert your data as described above. You can also [contact Support](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/support/ticket) to migrate back.
* **Migrate any pod-based indexes** whose data you want to keep. [Migrate each one to serverless](/guides/indexes/pods/migrate-a-pod-based-index-to-serverless) and finish creating the new serverless index before you start the downgrade, because the migration saves your index as a collection and the downgrade deletes all collections.
* **Move any `eu`-region assistants you want to keep to `us`.** [Recreate them in `us`](/guides/assistant/create-assistant) and re-upload their files. `eu` assistants you don't move are deleted.
* **Disconnect your organization's [SSO connection](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-single-sign-on-sso).**
* **Reassign or remove members** whose [organization role](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) isn't available on the Starter plan.
* **Get under the Starter storage limits.** Starter allows no more than 2 GB of data across your serverless indexes and 1 GB of assistant storage. Do this last, after the migrations above, because they can briefly leave a second copy of an index. [Delete records](/guides/manage-data/delete-data) and [assistant files](/guides/assistant/manage-files#delete-a-file) to fit.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You don't need to bring [Assistant usage](/guides/assistant/pricing-and-limits) (ingestion units, chat tokens, and context tokens) under Starter caps before downgrading. If you exceed Starter limits after downgrading, new requests may be blocked until usage is within limits.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you're switching from Standard to Builder instead of Starter, your organization must be under the [Builder plan quotas](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits). You must also delete all backups and remove or stop any features not available on Builder, such as bulk import, pod-based indexes, storage integrations, RBAC, and SSO.

## Limits

* Each organization is allowed only one trial.
* Organizations already on a Standard or Enterprise plan can't activate a Standard plan trial.
* Organizations that initially subscribed to Pinecone through marketplace partners can't activate a Standard plan trial.

If you have questions, [contact Support](https://www.pinecone.io/contact/support/).


# Upgrade your billing plan
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/billing/upgrade-billing-plan

Upgrade your Pinecone organization to the Builder, Standard, or Enterprise plan and pay by card or through a cloud marketplace.

This page describes how to upgrade to a paid [Builder, Standard, or Enterprise plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/), either from the free Starter plan or from Builder to Standard or Enterprise. You can pay with a credit or debit card, or through a supported cloud marketplace if your organization is on the Starter plan.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To change your plan, you must be an [organization owner or billing admin](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles).

> [!TIP]
>
> To evaluate the Standard plan before you start paying, see the [Standard plan trial](/admin/billing/standard-trial). You get 21 days and \$300 in credits. Each organization can activate one trial, and [some organizations aren't eligible](/admin/billing/standard-trial#limits).

> [!TIP]
>
> To commit to annual spending, [contact Pinecone](https://www.pinecone.io/contact).

## Upgrade to the Builder plan

The Builder plan is a flat \$20/month plan with higher quotas than Starter and no usage overages. To upgrade from Starter to Builder:

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. Click **Upgrade** in the **Builder** plan section.
3. If you have a promo code, click **Add discount code** and enter it. For details, see [Redeem a promo code](/admin/billing/redeem-a-promo-code).
4. Click **Continue**.
5. Enter your credit or debit card information.
6. Click **Upgrade**.

After upgrading, your organization is immediately on the Builder plan with the higher [Builder plan quotas](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits). If you need additional capacity or features not included in Builder, you can [upgrade to Standard or Enterprise](#upgrade-to-the-standard-or-enterprise-plan) at any time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The [Builder plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) is available with credit/debit card billing only and isn't supported through cloud marketplaces.

## Upgrade to the Standard or Enterprise plan

### Pay with a credit/debit card

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. Click **Upgrade** in the **Standard** or **Enterprise** plan section.
3. Click **Credit / Debit card**.
4. Enter your credit card information.
5. Click **Upgrade**.

After upgrading, you'll immediately start paying for usage of your Pinecone indexes, including the serverless indexes that were free on the Starter plan. For more details about how costs are calculated, see [Understand Pinecone cost](/guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost).

### Pay through the Google Cloud Marketplace

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. Click **Upgrade** in the **Standard** or **Enterprise** plan section.
3. Click **Billing through GCP**. This takes you to the [Pinecone listing](https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/pinecone-public/pinecone) in the Google Cloud Marketplace.
4. Click **Subscribe**.
5. On the **Order Summary** page, select a billing account, accept the terms and conditions, and click **Subscribe**.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > The billing unit listed doesn't reflect the actual cost or metering of costs for Pinecone. See the [Pinecone Pricing page](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) for accurate details.
6. On the **Your order request has been sent to Pinecone** modal, click **Sign up with Pinecone**. This takes you to a Google-specific Pinecone login page.
7. Log in to your Pinecone account. Use the same authentication method as your existing Pinecone organization.
8. Select an organization from the list. You can only connect to organizations that are on the [Starter plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/). You can also create a new organization.
9. Click **Connect to Pinecone** and follow the prompts.

After your organization is connected and upgraded, you'll receive a confirmation message. You'll then immediately start paying for usage of your Pinecone indexes, including the serverless indexes that were free on the Starter plan. For more details about how costs are calculated, see [Understand Pinecone cost](/guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost).

### Pay through the AWS Marketplace

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. Click **Upgrade** in the **Standard** or **Enterprise** plan section.
3. Click **Billing through AWS**. This takes you to the [Pinecone listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-xhgyscinlz4jk) in the AWS Marketplace.
4. Click **View purchase options**.
5. On the **Subscribe to Pinecone Vector Database** page, review the offer and then click **Subscribe**.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > The billing unit listed doesn't reflect the actual cost or metering of costs for Pinecone. See the [Pinecone Pricing page](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) for accurate details.
6. You'll see a message stating that your subscription is in process. Click **Set up your account**. This takes you to an AWS-specific Pinecone login page.

   > [!WARNING]
   >
   > If the [Pinecone subscription page](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/saas/ordering?productId=738798c3-eeca-494a-a2a9-161bee9450b2) shows a message stating, “You are currently subscribed to this offer,” contact your team members to request an invitation to the existing AWS-linked organization. The **Set up your account** button is clickable, but Pinecone doesn't create a new AWS-linked organization.
7. Log in to your Pinecone account. Use the same authentication method as your existing Pinecone organization.
8. Select an organization from the list. You can only connect to organizations that are on the [Starter plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/). You can also create a new organization.
9. Click **Connect to Pinecone** and follow the prompts.

After your organization is connected and upgraded, you'll receive a confirmation message. You'll then immediately start paying for usage of your Pinecone indexes, including the serverless indexes that were free on the Starter plan. For more details about how costs are calculated, see [Understand Pinecone cost](/guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost).

### Pay through the Microsoft Marketplace

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Billing > Plans**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/billing/plans).
2. Click **Upgrade** in the **Standard** or **Enterprise** plan section.
3. Click **Billing through Azure**. This takes you to the [Pinecone listing](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/product/saas/pineconesystemsinc1688761585469.pineconesaas) in the Microsoft Marketplace.
4. Click **Get it now**.
5. Select the **Pinecone - Pay As You Go** plan.
6. Click **Subscribe**.
7. On the **Subscribe to Pinecone** page, select the required details and click **Review + subscribe**.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > The billing unit listed doesn't reflect the actual cost or metering of costs for Pinecone. See the [Pinecone Pricing page](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/) for accurate details.
8. Click **Subscribe**.
9. After the subscription is approved, click **Configure account now**. This redirects you to a Microsoft-specific Pinecone login page.
10. Log in to your Pinecone account. Use the same authentication method as your existing Pinecone organization.
11. Select an organization from the list. You can only connect to organizations that are on the [Starter plan](https://www.pinecone.io/pricing/). You can also create a new organization.
12. Click **Connect to Pinecone** and follow the prompts.

After your organization is connected and upgraded, you'll receive a confirmation message. You'll then immediately start paying for usage of your Pinecone indexes, including the serverless indexes that were free on the Starter plan. For more details about how costs are calculated, see [Understand Pinecone cost](/guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost).


# Delete your organization
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/organizations/delete-your-organization

Permanently delete a Pinecone organization after you delete its indexes, collections, and projects and downgrade to the Starter plan.

Before you can delete your Pinecone organization, you need to delete all of its projects and downgrade to the Starter plan. To delete a project, first delete its indexes and collections.

* [Delete an index](/guides/manage-data/manage-indexes#delete-an-index)
* [Delete a project](/admin/projects/manage-projects#delete-a-project)
* [Downgrade to the Starter plan](/admin/billing/downgrade-billing-plan)

Once you've downgraded to the Starter plan and deleted your indexes and projects, you can delete your organization.

> [!WARNING]
>
> This action cannot be undone.

1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**Settings > Manage**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/manage).
2. Click **Delete this organization**.
3. Type the organization name and confirm the deletion.


# Create a project
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/projects/create-a-project

Create a new Pinecone project in your organization using the console or Admin API, including project name, tags, and customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).

If you're an [organization owner or organization manager](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles), you can create a project in your organization.

> [tab] Pinecone console
>
> 1. In the Pinecone console, go to [**your profile > Organization settings > Projects**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/settings/projects).
>
> 2. Click **+ Create project**.
>
> 3. Enter a project name in **Give your project a name**.
>
>    > [!NOTE]
>    >
>    > A project name can contain up to 512 characters. For more information, see [Object identifiers](/reference/api/database-limits/identifier-limits).
>
> 4. (Optional) Tags are key-value pairs that you can use to categorize and identify the project. To add a tag, click **+ Add tag** and enter a tag key and value.
>
> 5. (Optional, Enterprise plan) Turn on **Enforce customer managed encryption (CMEK)**. For more information, see [Configure CMEK](/guides/production/configure-cmek).
>
> 6. Click **Create project**.
>
>    To create an index from a sample movies dataset, go to **Database > Quickstart** and click **Load from dataset**.
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > The number of projects per organization varies by plan. For details, see [Projects per organization](/reference/api/database-limits/object-limits). To create additional projects, [upgrade your plan](/admin/billing/upgrade-billing-plan).

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
>
> curl "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/projects" \
>     -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
> 	-H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
> 	-d '{
>           "name":"example-project"
>         }'
> ```
>
> ```bash CLI theme={null}
> # Target the organization for which you want to 
> # create a project.
> pc target -o "example-org"
> # Create the project and set it as the target 
> # project for the CLI.
> pc project create -n "example-project" --target
> ```
>
> The example returns a response like the following:
>
> ```json curl theme={null}
> {
>   "id": "32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2",
>   "name": "example-project",
>   "max_pods": 0,
>   "force_encryption_with_cmek": false,
>   "organization_id": "-NM7af6f234168c4e44a",
>   "created_at": "2025-03-16T22:46:45.030Z"
> }
> ```
>
> ```text CLI theme={null}
> [SUCCESS] Project example-cli-project created successfully.
>
> ATTRIBUTE           VALUE
> Name                example-project
> ID                  32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2
> Organization ID     -NM7af6f234168c4e44a
> Created At          2025-10-27 23:27:46.370088 +0000 UTC
> Force Encryption    false
> Max Pods            5
>
> [SUCCESS] Target project set to example-cli-project
> ```

## Next steps

* [Add users to your project](/admin/projects/manage-project-members#add-members-to-a-project)
* [Create an index](/guides/index-data/create-an-index)
* [Create an assistant](/guides/assistant/create-assistant)


# Manage API keys
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/projects/manage-api-keys

Create, view, update, and delete Pinecone API keys with custom permissions per project, including scoped roles and data plane access controls.

Each Pinecone [project](/admin/projects/understanding-projects) has one or more API keys. To [make calls to the Pinecone API](/guides/get-started/quickstart), you must provide a valid API key for the relevant Pinecone project.

This page shows you how to [create](#create-an-api-key), [view](#view-project-api-keys), [update](#update-an-api-key), and [delete](#delete-an-api-key) API keys.

> [!WARNING]
>
> If you use custom API key permissions, make sure you [target your index by host](/guides/manage-data/target-an-index#target-by-index-host-recommended) when performing data operations such as `upsert` and `query`.

## Create an API key

> [tab] Pinecone console
>
> 1. Open the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects).
>
> 2. Select your project.
>
> 3. Go to **API keys**.
>
> 4. Click **+ API key**.
>
> 5. Enter an **API key name**.
>
> 6. Select the **Permissions** to grant to the API key. For a description of the permission roles, see [Project roles](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles).
>
>    > [!NOTE]
>    >
>    > Users on the Starter and Builder plans can set the permissions to **All** only. To customize the permissions further, [upgrade to the Standard or Enterprise plan](/admin/billing/upgrade-billing-plan).
>
> 7. Click **Create key**.
>
> 8. Copy and save the generated API key in a secure place for future use.
>
>    > [!WARNING]
>    >
>    > You cannot view the API key again after you close the dialog.
>
> 9. Click **Close**.

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> PINECONE_PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
> PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
>
> curl -X POST "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/projects/$PINECONE_PROJECT_ID/api-keys" \
>      -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
>      -d '{
>            "name": "example-api-key",
>            "roles": ["ProjectEditor"]
>          }'
> ```
>
> ```bash CLI theme={null}
> # Target the project for which you want to create an API key.
> pc target -o "example-org" -p "example-project"
> # Create the API key
> pc api-key create -n "example-api-key" --roles ProjectEditor
> ```
>
> The example returns a response like the following:
>
> ```json curl theme={null}
> {
>   "key": {
>     "id": "62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88",
>     "name": "example-api-key",
>     "project_id": "32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2",
>     "roles": [
>       "ProjectEditor"
>     ],
>     "created_at": "2025-10-20T23:40:27.069075Z"
>   },
>   "value": "..."
> }
> ```
>
> ```text CLI theme={null}
> ATTRIBUTE     VALUE
> Name          example-api-key
> ID            62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88
> Value         ...
> Project ID    32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2
> Roles         ProjectEditor
> ```

> 2. Select your project.
> 3. Go to the **API keys** tab.
>
> You'll see a list of all API keys for the project, including their names, creation dates, creators, partial values, and permissions.

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]

> > To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).

> curl -X GET "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/projects/$PINECONE_PROJECT_ID/api-keys" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \

>

## View API key details

> [tab] Code

> ```
>
> ```bash CLI theme={null}
> PINECONE_API_KEY_ID="62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88"

> ```
>
> The example returns a response like the following:

> Roles         ProjectEditor
> ```

## Update an API key

> [!NOTE]
>
> Users on the Starter and Builder plans can't change API key permissions once they're set. Instead, [create a new API key](#create-an-api-key) or [upgrade to the Standard or Enterprise plan](/admin/billing/upgrade-billing-plan).

If you're a [project owner](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles), you can update an API key's permissions. To rename a key, use the API.

> [tab] Pinecone console
>
> 1. Open the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects).
>
> 2. Select your project.
>
> 3. Go to the **API keys** tab.
>
> 4. In the row of the API key you want to change, in the **Actions** column, click **ellipsis (...) menu > Settings**.
>
> 5. Change the permissions for the API key as needed.
>
>    For information about the different API key permissions, see [Project roles](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles).
>
> 6. Click **Update**.

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> PINECONE_API_KEY_ID="62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88"
> PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
>
> curl -X PATCH "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/api-keys/$PINECONE_API_KEY_ID" \
>      -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
>      -d '{
>            "name": "new-api-key-name",
>            "roles": ["ProjectEditor"]
>          }'
> ```
>
> ```bash CLI theme={null}
> PINECONE_API_KEY_ID="62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88"
>
> # Target the organization that contains the API key.
> pc target -o "example-org"
> # Update the API key name.
> pc api-key update -i $PINECONE_API_KEY_ID -n "new-api-key-name"
> ```
>
> The example returns a response like the following:
>
> ```json curl theme={null}
> {
>   "id": "62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88",
>   "name": "new-api-key-name",
>   "project_id": "32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2",
>   "roles": [
>     "ProjectEditor"
>   ],
>   "created_at": "2025-10-22T19:27:21.202955Z"
> }
> ```
>
> ```text CLI theme={null}
> ATTRIBUTE     VALUE
> Name          new-api-key-name
> ID            62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88
> Project ID    32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2
> Roles         ProjectEditor
> ```

## Delete an API key

If you're a [project owner](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles), you can delete an API key.

> [tab] Pinecone console
>
> 1. Open the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects).
> 2. Select your project.
> 3. Go to the **API keys** tab.
> 4. In the row of the API key you want to change, in the **Actions** column, click **ellipsis (...) menu > Delete**.
> 5. Enter the **API key name**.
> 6. Click **Delete API key**.
>
>    > [!WARNING]
>    >
>    > Deleting an API key is irreversible and immediately disables any applications using the API key.

> [tab] Code
>
> > [!NOTE]
> >
> > To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).
>
> ```bash curl theme={null}
> PINECONE_API_KEY_ID="62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88"
> PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
>
> curl -X DELETE "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/api-keys/$PINECONE_API_KEY_ID" \
>      -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
>      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN"
> ```
>
> ```bash CLI theme={null}
> PINECONE_API_KEY_ID="62b0dbfe-3489-4b79-b850-34d911527c88"
>
> # Delete the API key. Use --skip-confirmation to skip
> # the confirmation prompt.
> pc api-key delete -i $PINECONE_API_KEY_ID
> ```
>
> The example returns a response like the following:
>
> ```text curl theme={null}
> No response payload
> ```
>
> ```text CLI theme={null}
> [WARN] This operation will delete API key example-api-key from project example-project.
> [WARN] Any integrations that authenticate with this API key will immediately stop working.
> [WARN] This action cannot be undone.
> Do you want to continue? (y/N): y
> [INFO] You chose to continue delete.
> [SUCCESS] API key example-api-key deleted
> ```


# Manage project members
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/projects/manage-project-members

Add, remove, and update Pinecone project members using role-based access control (RBAC) to manage permissions and project owner roles.

[Organization owners](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) or [project owners](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles) can manage members in a project. Each member is assigned one or more [project roles](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles) that determine their permissions within the project.

To assign and manage roles programmatically with the Admin API, or to manage roles for service accounts and API keys, see [Manage roles and access](/admin/security/manage-rbac).

> [!TIP]
>
> For information about managing members at the organization level, see [Manage organization members](/admin/organizations/manage-organization-members).

## Add members to a project

> [!NOTE]
>
> Project owners can add existing organization members to a project and manage their project roles. Only [organization owners](/admin/organizations/understanding-organizations#organization-roles) can invite people who aren't yet members of the organization.

You can add members to a project in the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects):

1. Select your project.
2. Go to [**Settings > Access**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects/-/access/members) and select the **Members** tab.
3. Enter the member's email address or name.
4. Select a [**Project role**](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles) for the member. The role determines the member's permissions within Pinecone.
5. Click **Invite**.

If the person is already a member of your organization, they get access to the project right away. Otherwise, Pinecone emails them an invite, and they join your organization as an organization member, with access to the project, when they accept it.

## Change a member's role

You can change a member's role in the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects):

1. Select your project.
2. Go to [**Settings > Access**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects/-/access/members) and select the **Members** tab.
3. In the row of the member you want to edit, click **ellipsis (...) menu > Edit role**.
4. Select a [**Project role**](/admin/projects/understanding-projects#project-roles) for the member.
5. Click **Save**.

## Remove a member

You can remove a member from a project in the [Pinecone console](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects):

1. Select your project.
2. Go to [**Settings > Access**](https://app.pinecone.io/organizations/-/projects/-/access/members) and select the **Members** tab.
3. In the row of the member you want to remove, click **ellipsis (...) menu > Remove from project**.
4. Click **Remove member**.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To remove yourself from a project, in your user's row, click **ellipsis (...) menu > Leave project** and confirm.


# Manage projects
Source: https://docs.pinecone.io/admin/projects/manage-projects

View project details, rename projects, and delete projects in your Pinecone organization using the console or Admin API with owner permissions.

This page shows you how to view project details, rename a project, and delete a project.

> [!NOTE]

## View project details

This example retrieves the details of a project:

> [!NOTE]
>
> To complete this action through the Admin API, you need an [access token](/admin/organizations/manage-service-accounts#retrieve-an-access-token).

```bash curl theme={null}
PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
PROJECT_ID="32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2"

curl -X GET "https://api.pinecone.io/admin/projects/$PROJECT_ID" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $PINECONE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
     -H "X-Pinecone-Api-Version: 2026-07" \
     -H "accept: application/json"
```

```bash CLI theme={null}
PROJECT_ID="32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2"

# Target the organization that contains the project.
pc target -o "example-org" 
# Fetch the project details.
pc project describe -i $PROJECT_ID
```

The example returns a response like the following:

```json curl theme={null}

  "id": "32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2",

  "organization_id": "-NM7af6f234168c4e44a",
  "created_at": "2025-10-27T23:27:46.370088Z"
}
```

```text CLI theme={null}
ATTRIBUTE           VALUE
Name                example-project
ID                  32c8235a-5220-4a80-a9f1-69c24109e6f2
Organization ID     -NM7af6f234168c4e44a
Created At          2025-10-27 23:27:46.370088 +0000 UTC
```
